description:
File: crate-jmap-chat-server/src/memory.rs:430-432

  #[derive(Debug)]
  pub struct MemoryError(pub String);

The 'memory' feature is documented as 'API stability is opt-in via
this feature and may break across minor versions while the crate is
pre-1.0' (lib.rs:25-27, memory.rs:21-23). That is a written-down
intent but not a Rust-level enforcement. Downstream consumer
crates that use MemoryBackend (this workspace's test suite, the
jmap-testjig binary, and any third party building demos against
the docs) match on MemoryError(s) literally — that match shape is
the type's contract whether the rustdoc says 'unstable' or not.

Specific footguns:

1. Adding a #[source] error chain (anyhow style or std-Error
   source(): ergonomic for real-world debugging) requires
   reshaping the tuple. Every match site breaks.

2. The pub field makes the string-allocation choice part of the
   contract: callers can read the unbounded String at any time.
   Switching to Cow<'static, str> or a small-string optimization
   variant is breaking.

3. Other reference impls in this workspace follow the same
   pattern (will need a canonical-template sweep) so the breakage
   cost compounds.

Fix:
  #[non_exhaustive]
  #[derive(Debug)]
  pub struct MemoryError {
      message: String,
  }

  impl MemoryError {
      pub fn new(s: impl Into<String>) -> Self { ... }
      pub fn message(&self) -> &str { ... }
  }

Plus #[non_exhaustive] on the struct. The Display impl already
goes through self.0 / self.message — Display callers see no
difference. Tests that pattern-match on the tuple field migrate
to .message().

The 'pre-1.0 minor break is OK' policy is the right escape valve
if a consumer needs structured error chaining urgently, but every
break costs propagation churn at every downstream crate. Better
to land the shape that future-proofs both fronts at once.
title: API contract: MemoryError exposes pub String tuple field
